about: Genetic testing and population health company, Color, based in South San Francisco, which offers hereditary cancer screening and helps employers, health systems and governments run genetic and cancer care programmes at scale, including its COVID-19 testing and vaccination sites. Founded in 2015 by Elad Gil and Othman Laraki. Customers are employers and healthcare organisations, with some direct-to-consumer tests. B2B-focused brand with a moderate profile in US healthcare.

South Korean biotech company based in Seongnam, developing drug delivery technology, including its DrugFluidic and ECO-Fluidic microsphere platforms for sustained-release injectable medicines, working with pharmaceutical partners on licensed products. Listed on the KOSDAQ market. Revenue is mainly from licensing and development milestones, and it has no consumer brand. B2B pharma platform company, little known beyond the biotech sector and unlikely to see value in consumer sponsorship.
cb_desc: Inventory Lab is a Next- generation drug delivery...

about: Developer of cell culture devices, best known for the G-Rex bioreactor flasks used to grow immune cells and other cells for cell and gene therapy research and manufacturing, based in the Minneapolis-St Paul area. Customers are biotech companies, academic labs and cell therapy developers, mostly in the US, buying the flasks as consumable products. B2B life-science tools brand with strong standing among cell therapy scientists but none among consumers.
cb_desc: Wilson Wolf develops innovative mammalian cell culture devices.

about: US medical device company, Tivic Health Systems, listed on Nasdaq (TIVC), which sells ClearUP, a handheld bioelectronic device for sinus pain and congestion relief, sold directly to consumers online and through retailers. The record shows San Antonio, while the company is more commonly associated with California. Revenue is small and the company has restructured. Consumer health brand with limited awareness.

Galapagos is a Belgian biotechnology company based in Mechelen, founded in 1999 and listed on Euronext Brussels and Nasdaq (GLPG). It discovered filgotinib, marketed as Jyseleca for rheumatoid arthritis and ulcerative colitis through its Gilead partnership, and built a CAR-T cell therapy business with decentralized manufacturing. Gilead paid $5 billion upfront in 2019 for rights and a stake. After setbacks it ended the Gilead collaboration on Jyseleca and in 2025 moved to wind down cell therapy. Revenue is collaboration-driven, employees number in the hundreds, and consumer awareness is low.

Horizon Pharma, later Horizon Therapeutics plc, was an Irish-domiciled biopharmaceutical company with major operations in Deerfield, Illinois, focused on rare, autoimmune and severe inflammatory diseases. Its main medicines were Tepezza for thyroid eye disease, Krystexxa for chronic gout and Uplizna, sold to specialist physicians and hospitals, mainly in the United States, and generating over 3 billion dollars of annual sales. It was listed on Nasdaq as HZNP. Amgen acquired the company for about 27.8 billion dollars in October 2023. Brand awareness is among prescribers, not consumers.

ANGUS Chemical is a specialty chemical producer, headquartered in Buffalo Grove, Illinois, making nitroalkanes and derivatives such as amino alcohols, oxazolidines and biocides used in paints and coatings, metalworking fluids, personal care, pharmaceutical intermediates and water treatment. Customers are industrial manufacturers, who buy it through long supply contracts. It runs a production site in Sterlington, Louisiana, and has changed ownership several times, with Dow owning it for a long period before a later private-equity sale, so current ownership should be checked. B2B ingredient supplier with low consumer visibility.
cb_desc: Angus Chemical specialty and fine chemical company..

about: BGI Group is a Shenzhen-based genomics company founded in 1999 and a major player in DNA sequencing. Through listed units MGI Tech and BGI Genomics, it sells sequencers and reagents, runs genetic testing services including the NIFTY prenatal test, large population-genomics projects and COVID-19 tests. Customers are hospitals, research institutes, governments and labs in over 100 countries. The US placed several BGI entities on trade restriction lists, which complicates western partnerships. B2B and medical brand, with limited consumer recognition outside China, though a large organisation with thousands of employees.

EQRx was a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company founded by Alexis Borisy that aimed to develop and sell cancer and immunology drugs at much lower prices than existing therapies. Its pipeline included aumolertinib for lung cancer, licensed from Hansoh Pharma, and other small molecules in partnership with Chinese developers. It listed on Nasdaq via a SPAC merger in December 2021, raising over 1.8 billion dollars. In 2023 it agreed to merge with Revolution Medicines and the deal closed in November 2023. Never had a commercial product, so brand awareness was limited to biotech and investor circles.

Invitae was a San Francisco genetic testing company that offered clinical genetic panels for hereditary cancer, rare disease and reproductive health, plus oncology and consumer-facing genetics through its Ciitizen patient-records business. Customers were doctors, hospitals and patients, billed through insurers and direct payment. It listed on the NYSE (NVTA) in 2015, expanded through acquisitions such as Genelex and ArcherDX, and reached over 500 million dollars in annual revenue. It filed for Chapter 11 in February 2024 and its main assets were acquired by Labcorp in 2024. Known in healthcare, with little general consumer brand awareness.

SAGE Therapeutics was a Cambridge, Massachusetts neuroscience biopharma that developed Zulresso for postpartum depression, the first approved treatment of its kind, and Zurzuvae, an oral pill co-commercialised with Biogen from 2023. Customers are psychiatrists and obstetric care providers, with revenue from product sales and collaboration payments. Founded in 2010 and listed on Nasdaq (SAGE), it struggled after failed depression and Alzheimer's-related trials and cut staff. Supernus Pharmaceuticals agreed to acquire it in 2025 for roughly 795 million dollars. Brand awareness is among doctors, but Zurzuvae has a patient-facing marketing campaign.

Seagen, formerly Seattle Genetics, was a Bothell, Washington biotechnology company and a pioneer in antibody-drug conjugates for cancer. Its marketed products were Adcetris for lymphoma, Padcev for bladder cancer, Tivdak for cervical cancer and Tukysa for breast cancer, sold to oncologists worldwide with annual revenue of roughly 2 billion dollars. Founded in 1998 and listed on Nasdaq (SGEN), it was acquired by Pfizer for about 43 billion dollars, closing in December 2023, and now operates inside Pfizer Oncology. Brand awareness is among cancer specialists and investors.

Assertio is a US specialty pharmaceutical company, based in Lake Forest, Illinois, that acquires and sells branded medicines mainly for pain, neurology and inflammatory conditions. Products include Indocin suppositories and suspension, Otrexup (methotrexate auto-injector), Sympazan, Zipsor, Cambia and Rolvedon for neutropenia, sold to pharmacies and hospitals via wholesalers, with revenue of roughly 100 to 150 million dollars a year. Listed on Nasdaq (ASRT), it merged with Spectrum Pharmaceuticals in 2023 and has had heavy generic competition and debt restructuring. Brand awareness is among prescribers, not consumers.
cb_desc: Assertio develops and commercializes prescription...

about: IVERIC bio was a New Jersey ophthalmology biopharmaceutical company focused on retinal diseases. Its key product, Izervay (avacincaptad pegol), was approved by the FDA in 2023 as the second treatment for geographic atrophy, an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, injected by retina specialists. Previously named Ophthotech, it listed on Nasdaq as ISEE. Astellas Pharma acquired it in 2023 for about 5.9 billion dollars, so it now operates as part of Astellas. Brand awareness is limited to eye doctors and healthcare investors, not consumers.

Taibang Biological Group is a Chinese plasma products company, tied to Shandong Taibang Biological Products, that collects human plasma at its own donation stations and produces human albumin, immunoglobulins and clotting factors. Customers are hospitals and distributors in China, supplied under heavy government regulation. It grew out of the former Nasdaq-listed China Biologic Products, which went private in 2020 and later restructured under Chinese ownership. Headquartered in Beijing, it is a large domestic plasma fractionator with thousands of employees. B2B healthcare brand, little consumer recognition, though known within Chinese hospital supply.
cb_desc: Taibang Biologic Group is a Chinese biopharmaceutical..

about: ViewRay was a medical device company based near Cleveland, Ohio, that made the MRIdian, an MRI-guided radiation therapy system that lets oncologists see tumours in real time while treating them. Customers were hospitals and cancer centres, with revenue from system sales, installation and service contracts across the US, Europe and Asia, and annual revenue of roughly 100 million dollars. It listed on Nasdaq (VRAY) in 2016 via a merger, struggled with cash burn and filed for bankruptcy in July 2023, with assets acquired by a successor. Brand known to radiation oncology staff, not consumers.

CymaBay Therapeutics was a California biopharmaceutical company, based in Newark, developing treatments for liver and rare metabolic diseases. Its lead drug, seladelpar, a PPAR-delta agonist for primary biliary cholangitis, showed strong late-stage results and was approved by the FDA in 2024 as Livdelzi. It was listed on Nasdaq (CBAY) and had no marketed product before the sale. Gilead Sciences acquired it for about 4.3 billion dollars, completed in March 2024. Brand awareness is among hepatologists and investors only, with no consumer profile.

IGM Biosciences was a Mountain View, California biotechnology company developing engineered IgM antibodies for cancer and autoimmune disease. Its lead candidate, imvotamab, targeted CD20 in lupus and other autoimmune conditions, and it worked with Sanofi on cancer programmes. Listed on Nasdaq as IGMS, it never had an approved product and burned substantial cash. In early 2025 it discontinued its clinical programmes, cut most staff and explored strategic options. Brand awareness was limited to biotech investors and specialist physicians, with no consumer recognition.
cb_desc: IGM Biosciences is a biotechnology company that...

about: MorphoSys was a German biotechnology company based in Planegg near Munich, known for antibody technology and for Monjuvi (tafasitamab) for lymphoma, marketed with Incyte, plus the myelofibrosis drug candidate pelabresib. It was listed on Nasdaq and Frankfurt (MOR) and earned money from royalties on partnered antibody discovery, such as Tremfya, and product sales. After acquiring Constellation Pharmaceuticals in 2021 it carried large losses. Novartis acquired MorphoSys for about 2.7 billion euros, completed in May 2024. Brand awareness is among oncologists and biotech investors, with no consumer profile.

Pliant Therapeutics is a South San Francisco clinical-stage biotechnology company developing treatments for fibrotic diseases. Its lead candidate, bexotegrast, a dual integrin inhibitor, was tested in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and primary sclerosing cholangitis, partnered earlier with Novartis. Listed on Nasdaq (PLRX), it has no marketed product and earns no product revenue. In 2025 its main trial was halted after safety concerns and the programme discontinued, leading to restructuring. Brand awareness is within biotech and investor circles, with none among consumers.

Shockwave Medical is a Santa Clara, California medical device company that makes intravascular lithotripsy systems, which use sonic pressure waves delivered through a catheter to break up calcified plaque in arteries, mainly in the heart and legs. Customers are hospitals and interventional cardiologists, with revenue from single-use catheters and generators, reaching roughly 730 million dollars in 2023. It listed on Nasdaq (SWAV) in 2019. Johnson & Johnson acquired it for about 13.1 billion dollars, closing in May 2024, and it now sits inside J&J MedTech. Brand awareness is among cardiologists, not consumers.

Arcellx is a clinical-stage biotechnology company, founded in 2014 and based in Maryland with roots in Redwood City, California, developing CAR-T cell therapies for cancer. Its lead product, anitocabtagene autoleucel (anito-cel) for multiple myeloma, is being commercialised under a collaboration with Kite, a Gilead company, which shares costs and profits. Customers will be cancer hospitals and haematologists. Listed on Nasdaq (ACLX) since 2022, it earns collaboration income rather than product sales so far. Brand awareness is limited to oncology and investor communities, with no consumer profile.

Becton Dickinson India is the Indian subsidiary of BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company), the Franklin Lakes, New Jersey medical technology group listed on the NYSE (BDX). BD makes syringes, needles, IV catheters, diagnostic instruments, specimen collection and infusion pumps, sold to hospitals, labs and health systems, with annual revenue around 20 billion dollars and roughly 70,000 employees. The Indian unit sells and manufactures disposable devices locally. In 2025 BD agreed to merge its biosciences and diagnostics business with Waters. Strong in healthcare supply, but little consumer awareness.

Nimbus Therapeutics is a Boston-based biotechnology company founded in 2009 that uses computational physics-based modelling to design small-molecule drugs against hard targets. Its TYK2 inhibitor programme was sold to Takeda in 2022 in a deal worth up to 6 billion dollars including 4 billion dollars upfront, and it continues to pursue cancer and metabolic programmes such as ACC and WRN inhibitors. It is venture-backed and privately held, with investors including Atlas Venture and Bill Gates-linked funds. B2B science brand with recognition only among pharma and investors.
cb_desc: Nimbus Therapeutics uses computational technology to.

about: RefleXion Medical is a Hayward, California medical technology company that makes the X1, a radiotherapy system combining a linear accelerator with PET imaging, called biology-guided radiotherapy, which lets the machine track tumours using their own emitted signals and treat multiple lesions. Customers are hospitals and cancer centres that buy systems and service contracts. Founded in 2009 by Sam Mazin, it is venture-backed and privately held, with the X1 cleared by the FDA. Brand awareness is among radiation oncologists, not consumers.

Syros Pharmaceuticals was a Watertown, Massachusetts biotechnology company that studied gene control to develop cancer medicines. Its lead candidate, tamibarotene, was being developed for myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukaemia, along with SY-2101 for acute promyelocytic leukaemia. Listed on Nasdaq (SYRS) after its 2016 IPO, it never had an approved product. After the pivotal MDS trial failed in 2024 it cut most staff, and it later explored strategic alternatives and wound down. Known only in oncology and investor circles, with no consumer profile.
cb_desc: Syros Pharmaceuticals is a life sciences company that focuse...

about: Adaptimmune is a UK-founded cell therapy company based in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, with a large US base in Pennsylvania, developing engineered T cell receptor therapies for solid tumours. Its Tecelra (afami-cel) was approved by the FDA in August 2024 for synovial sarcoma, the first engineered T cell receptor therapy for a solid tumour, and it has other candidates such as lete-cel. Listed on Nasdaq (ADAP), it had collaborations with GSK and Astellas. In 2025, facing cash needs, it sold its commercial assets to US WorldMeds. Brand awareness is among oncologists, with no consumer profile.

BioNexus Gene Lab is a Kuala Lumpur-based Malaysian company listed on Nasdaq (BGLC), operating in genomic testing and chemicals. Its Chemrex subsidiary distributes industrial chemicals across Southeast Asia and generates most of its revenue, while the genomics unit offers health screening, including blood-based tests aimed at cancer risk and preventive care. Customers are industrial buyers, clinics and individual patients. Small-cap, with revenue in the millions of dollars, and little brand awareness beyond Malaysia.
cb_desc: BioNexus Gene Lab Corp does non-invasive blood-based.

about: Encoded Therapeutics is a South San Francisco biotechnology company, founded in 2015, developing gene therapies that use regulatory DNA elements delivered with AAV vectors to switch genes on in the right cells, aimed mainly at severe genetic neurological disorders such as Dravet syndrome and other epilepsies. Its lead programme, ETX101, is in clinical testing. Customers would be neurologists and hospitals once approved. Privately held and venture-backed, with investors including Sofinnova and Fidelity and over 500 million dollars raised in total. Brand awareness is limited to biotech circles.
cb_desc: Encoded Therapeutics is a biotechnology company...

about: Evofem Biosciences is a San Diego women's health company whose only commercial product is Phexxi, a hormone-free vaginal gel contraceptive that regulates vaginal pH. It sells to women in the US through pharmacies, telehealth partners and direct-to-consumer advertising, and also promotes Soaanz, a heart-failure drug it acquired the rights to. It became public through a 2018 merger with Neothetics and was listed on Nasdaq (EVFM) before moving to over-the-counter trading. Revenue is in the tens of millions of dollars, with heavy debt. Consumer-facing brand with national advertising but modest awareness.
cb_desc: Evofem is a biopharmaceutical company that offers women...

about: Formation Bio is a New York-based pharmaceutical company, formerly Tech and Bio and earlier Triplet Therapeutics, that uses AI and data tools to speed drug development. Rather than doing early discovery, it buys or licenses assets from other developers and runs clinical development with its AI platform, working with Sanofi and OpenAI on tools. Founded in 2016 by Benjamin Liu, Tom Beadle and Chris Bohn, it raised a 372 million dollar Series D in 2024 from Andreessen Horowitz, Thrive and Sanofi, bringing total funding to over 500 million dollars. Privately held, known mainly in biotech and venture circles.

Metsera was a New York clinical-stage biotechnology company developing injectable and oral treatments for obesity and related conditions, built around monthly GLP-1 and amylin candidates such as MET-097i and MET-233i. Founded by ARCH Venture Partners and Population Health Partners, it listed on Nasdaq (MTSR) in January 2025 and had no approved drug. In November 2025 Pfizer acquired the company for up to about 10 billion dollars after a bidding contest with Novo Nordisk. Brand awareness is among investors and pharma, with none among consumers.

NGM Biopharmaceuticals was a South San Francisco biotechnology company researching therapies for liver, metabolic and retinal diseases, founded in 2007 with backing from Merck, which held a major collaboration and stake. Its pipeline included aldafermin for fatty liver disease, which failed in trials, and later antibody candidates for age-related eye disease and obesity. It was listed on Nasdaq (NGM) from 2019 and earned revenue from Merck collaboration payments. In 2024 it agreed to a take-private deal led by The Column Group and other investors, ending its public listing. Brand awareness only in biotech circles.
cb_desc: NGM Biopharmaceuticals is a drug discovery company...

about: Opthea is an Australian biotechnology company, based in Melbourne and listed on the ASX (OPT) with Nasdaq ADSs, developing sozinibercept, an injection used with standard anti-VEGF drugs for wet age-related macular degeneration. It ran two large Phase 3 trials, ShORe and COAST, and had financing and partnership arrangements with Carlyle and others. In early 2025 the trials failed to meet their main goals, which cut its value sharply and led to restructuring. Customers would have been retina specialists, and the company had no marketed product. Brand awareness is limited to ophthalmology and investor communities.
cb_desc: Opthea is a public Australian biotechnology company that...

about: PL Developments is a Westbury, New York manufacturer of private-label over-the-counter health products, including liquid and softgel medicines, vitamins and supplements, as well as personal care items, sold under retailers' own store brands, primarily to US drugstore, grocery and mass-market chains. It operates several US factories and distribution sites, with Time-Cap Labs a notable subsidiary, and employs thousands of people. Reported funding of about 500 million dollars is from October 2024 and is probably debt financing. B2B with essentially no consumer brand of its own. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: PL Developments manufactures, packages, and...

about: Regulus Therapeutics was a San Diego clinical-stage biotechnology company developing microRNA-targeted medicines. Its lead candidate, farabursen (RGLS8429), was in development for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, a genetic kidney condition, with Phase 3 plans after strong mid-stage data. It listed on Nasdaq (RGLS) and held a deal with Sanofi earlier in its life. Novartis agreed to acquire Regulus in April 2025 for up to 1.7 billion dollars, including milestone payments, and the deal closed that year. No marketed product and brand awareness limited to biotech and kidney disease specialists.

VBI Vaccines, formerly SciVac, was a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company developing vaccines and virus-like particle technology, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with research and manufacturing in Ottawa, Canada, and operations in Israel. Its main product, PreHevbrio, was a three-antigen hepatitis B vaccine for adults that was approved in the US in 2021. It also had COVID-19 and glioblastoma candidates. Listed on Nasdaq (VBIV), it ran into funding problems and in 2024 filed for creditor protection and sold off its assets. Customers were physicians and public health agencies. Brand awareness limited to healthcare and investors.
cb_desc: VBI Vaccines is a commercial stage biopharmaceutical..

about: Ventyx Biosciences is a San Diego clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing oral NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors and other small molecules for inflammatory disease, targeting conditions such as obesity-related inflammation, Parkinson's disease and cardiovascular disease. Founded in 2018 and listed on Nasdaq (VTYX), it has no approved product and relies on investor capital. Eli Lilly agreed in early 2026 to acquire the company for about 1.2 billion dollars. Customers would be specialist physicians once drugs are approved. Brand awareness is limited to pharma and investors, with no consumer profile.
cb_desc: Ventyx is a biopharmaceutical company focused on advancin...

about: Abeona Therapeutics is a Cleveland, Ohio gene and cell therapy company whose lead product, Zevaskyn (prademagene zamikeracel), received FDA approval in April 2025 for recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, a rare blistering skin disease. It uses patients' own gene-corrected skin cells grafted as sheets, and customers are specialised treatment centres paid through insurers at a price in the hundreds of thousands of dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (ABEO), it earlier explored AAV gene therapy programmes for eye and metabolic diseases. Brand awareness is among rare disease clinicians, patients and investors.

Akebia Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company focused on kidney disease. Its products are Vafseo (vadadustat), an oral drug for anaemia due to chronic kidney disease in dialysis patients, approved in the US in 2024, and Auryxia (ferric citrate) for phosphate control and iron deficiency. Customers are nephrologists and dialysis providers including large chains, with revenue from product sales of over 150 million dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (AKBA) and founded in 2007. Brand awareness is mostly among kidney specialists and investors, not consumers.

Apollo Therapeutics is a Cambridge, UK clinical-stage biotechnology company that develops drugs licensed from universities and large pharma partners, built as a shared-risk model with several big pharma backers, among them AstraZeneca, GSK and Johnson & Johnson. Its portfolio covers immunology, inflammation and metabolic diseases and includes antibody and small-molecule candidates in early and mid-stage trials. It has raised nearly 400 million dollars, including a large round in 2023, and is privately held. Customers would be physicians once products are approved. A B2B science company with recognition only in UK and global biotech circles.
cb_desc: Apollo Therapeutics is a portfolio biopharmaceutical...

about: Applied Therapeutics is a New York biopharmaceutical company developing treatments for rare metabolic diseases. Its lead candidate, govorestat (AT-007), an aldose reductase inhibitor, targets classic galactosemia and sorbitol dehydrogenase deficiency, and it also studied it for diabetic cardiomyopathy. The FDA declined to approve it for galactosemia in November 2024, leaving it with no marketed product and a restructuring. Founded in 2016 and listed on Nasdaq (APLT), it serves rare-disease specialists and families. Brand awareness is limited to patient communities and investors.

Areteia Therapeutics is a New Jersey-based biopharmaceutical company launched in 2023 with a large Series A, built around dexpramipexole, an oral drug for eosinophilic asthma, licensed from Knopp Biosciences. It has run Phase 3 trials in patients with uncontrolled asthma and plans other eosinophil-related diseases. Customers would be respiratory specialists and patients if approved. Privately held and venture-backed, with funding of about 425 million dollars. A B2B biotech with no meaningful consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Areteia Therapeutics is a biotechnology company...

about: BillionToOne is a Menlo Park, California molecular diagnostics company founded in 2016, known for Unity, a prenatal blood test that screens for genetic conditions in the fetus using small amounts of DNA, and Northstar, a liquid-biopsy test used to monitor cancer treatment. Customers are obstetricians, oncologists and health systems, paid mainly through insurers and direct billing, with revenue in the hundreds of millions of dollars and strong growth. It listed on Nasdaq (BLLN) in 2025. Brand awareness is among clinicians, with some patient-facing marketing for prenatal screening.
cb_desc: BillionToOne is a precision diagnostics company that....

about: Biodesix is a Colorado diagnostics company based in Louisville that makes blood-based tests for lung disease. Its main product is Nodify, a test pair that helps doctors decide whether lung nodules found on scans are likely cancer, along with the GeneStrat and Nodify Lung testing family, and it earns revenue from testing and from biopharma services work. Customers are physicians and health systems, billed through insurers and Medicare. Listed on Nasdaq (BDSX), with annual revenue of roughly 60 to 70 million dollars. Brand awareness is among pulmonologists.
cb_desc: Biodesix is a data-driven diagnostic solutions company..

about: Cellectis is a Paris-based biotechnology company, founded in 1999, that uses TALEN gene editing to create allogeneic CAR-T cell therapies off-the-shelf from healthy donor cells for blood cancers. It listed on Euronext Paris and Nasdaq (CLLS), and AstraZeneca is its largest shareholder after a 2023 investment. Other partners include Servier and Allogene, which licenses its UCART candidates, and it also has a plant gene editing unit. Customers would be haematology and oncology centres. Brand awareness is among cell therapy and biotech investors, not consumers.

F2G is a Manchester, UK biotechnology company developing antifungal drugs for life-threatening invasive infections, notably olorofim, a first-in-class drug against moulds such as Aspergillus that resist standard treatment. The FDA declined to approve olorofim in 2023, requesting more data, and the company continues the programme through a confirmatory trial. Founded in 2008 as a spin-out, it is private and venture-funded, with the most recent round in September 2024. Brand awareness is among infectious disease specialists.
cb_desc: F2G discovers and develops novel drugs for the treatment .

about: Guardian Pharmacy Services is an Atlanta, Georgia provider of medication management and pharmacy services for long-term care. It supplies prescriptions packaged by dose to assisted living, behavioural health and group homes, working through a network of roughly 50 pharmacies in over 40 states, and it generates about 1.2 billion dollars in annual revenue. Founded in 1983 and led by the Pittman and Dickinson families, it listed on the NYSE (GRDN) in September 2024. Customers are care facilities and residents. A B2B healthcare service brand with little consumer recognition. The Georgia country label refers to the US state.

Joincare Pharmaceutical Group is a Shenzhen-based Chinese pharmaceutical company, listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, that makes branded and generic medicines, active pharmaceutical ingredients and diagnostics. Its main areas are respiratory drugs including inhaled products, gastrointestinal products, and anti-infective drugs, and it controls the listed company Livzon Pharmaceutical. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and distributors across China, with some exports of ingredients. Annual revenue runs to several billion dollars. Mostly a B2B pharma brand, with a degree of consumer recognition in China through OTC products.
cb_desc: Joincare Pharmaceutical is a Pharmaceutical health care...

about: Mainstay Medical is a medical device company, founded in Ireland and listed on Euronext Paris before delisting, whose ReActiv8 implantable neurostimulation system treats chronic low back pain by stimulating nerves to the multifidus muscle to help restore control of the lower back. Customers are pain specialists and spine surgeons, with US commercial operations run from San Diego. The system holds FDA approval and CE marking. Revenue has been in the low tens of millions of dollars, with total funding of about 395 million dollars. Brand awareness is among doctors and patients with chronic back pain.
cb_desc: Mainstay Medical is a global medical device company that ...

about: Mereo BioPharma is a London and Redwood City biotechnology company, listed on Nasdaq (MREO), developing rare disease and oncology drugs. Its lead candidate setrusumab, an antibody against sclerostin, is being developed by partner Ultragenyx for osteogenesis imperfecta (brittle bone disease), with milestones and royalties owed to Mereo. It also has alvelestat for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency lung disease. The company has no marketed product, a small team and revenue from partnerships. Setrusumab's pivotal trial results in 2025 were disappointing for investors. Brand awareness is among rare disease clinicians and investors.
cb_desc: Mereo is a new UK-based speciality biopharmaceutical...

about: Molecular Templates was an Austin, Texas clinical-stage biotechnology company developing engineered toxin bodies, protein-based drugs that deliver a bacterial-derived toxin to kill cancer cells. Its candidates included MT-6402 and MT-5111 for HER2-positive cancers, and it had a partnership with Bristol Myers Squibb through Celgene, as well as with Takeda. Listed on Nasdaq (MTEM), it had no marketed product and struggled with funding, laying off staff in 2023 and 2024 and winding down operations soon after. Brand awareness was confined to biotech investors and oncology researchers.
cb_desc: Molecular Templates is a clinical-stage..

about: Quanta Dialysis Technologies is a Warwick, UK medical technology company that makes the SC+ haemodialysis system, a compact machine designed for use at home or in clinics, with a cartridge-based, easy-to-operate set-up. Founded in 2008, it has CE marking, UK approval and FDA clearance, and sells to dialysis providers, hospitals and national health services. Total funding is about 410 million dollars, with several private healthcare investors. It is private, with a small-to-mid-sized workforce. Brand awareness is among kidney specialists and renal care companies, not the public.
cb_desc: Quanta develops an advanced haemodialysis systems for us...

about: Scorpion Therapeutics was a Boston biotechnology company developing precision oncology medicines, notably STX-478, a mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor for breast and other cancers that spares healthy cells. Founded in 2020 by Keith Flaherty and others, it was backed by Third Rock Ventures and raised hundreds of millions of dollars from investors. Eli Lilly agreed to acquire it in January 2025 for up to 2.5 billion dollars, with the deal completed that year, and the programme continues inside Lilly. It had no marketed product and brand awareness was limited to biotech and oncology circles.

scPharmaceuticals is a Burlington, Massachusetts pharmaceutical company that developed and sells Furoscix, a subcutaneous infusion of furosemide delivered through an on-body device, to treat fluid congestion in heart failure and chronic kidney disease patients at home, avoiding hospital admission. Customers are cardiologists, hospitals and patients, billed through insurance. Listed on Nasdaq (SCPH), it reached roughly 60 million dollars in annual sales in 2024. MannKind agreed to acquire it in 2025 for about 360 million dollars. Brand awareness is among cardiologists and heart failure clinics.

Torrent Pharmaceuticals is an Indian drugmaker based in Ahmedabad and part of the Torrent Group, listed on the NSE and BSE. It specialises in chronic therapies, particularly cardiovascular, central nervous system, gastroenterology and diabetes medicines, and sells branded generics in India, Brazil, Germany, the US and other markets, with annual revenue of around 1 billion dollars or more. It acquired Curatio Healthcare in 2022 and moved to take majority control of JB Chemicals in 2025. Well known to Indian doctors and pharmacies, with strong visibility among OTC and prescription brands, though little recognition abroad.

TScan Therapeutics is a Waltham, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company developing T cell receptor engineered T cell therapies. Its lead programmes, TSC-101 and TSC-100, are aimed at preventing relapse in blood cancers such as acute myeloid leukaemia after stem cell transplant, and it also has solid-tumour candidates and a discovery platform to find T cell targets. Listed on Nasdaq (TCRX) since 2021, it is funded by investors and a partnership with Amgen and Novartis, and has no product revenue. Brand awareness is among cancer specialists and biotech investors.
cb_desc: TScan Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company..

about: ADARx Pharmaceuticals is a San Diego genetic medicine company developing RNA-based drugs, mainly small interfering RNA (siRNA) and RNA-editing therapies, delivered with its own chemistry and conjugation platform. Its programmes target cardiovascular, metabolic and neurological diseases, and it has collaborations with pharma partners. Founded in 2020 and venture-backed, it raised a large Series C in 2025, bringing total funding to about 332 million dollars. Privately held and pre-revenue, so customers would be physicians if medicines are approved. Brand awareness limited to RNA therapeutics and investor circles.
cb_desc: ADARx Pharmaceuticals is a genetic medicine company...

about: Alebund Pharmaceuticals is a Shanghai biopharmaceutical company, active in kidney and metabolic disease, developing treatments for chronic kidney disease complications. Its lead candidate AP301 is a phosphate binder, a drug for lowering high phosphate in dialysis patients and it is running late-stage studies in China with US plans. The FDA issued a complete response letter in 2025, delaying approval, and the company is pursuing further data.
